plan: Ten items with stems checked against the bank; takes ACT Math past 300. 3 hard (line-parabola sum, horizontal compression, circumscribed circle) / 2 medium / 5 easy.

A.rationale: 1/10 is one of the addends, not the sum.

candidates.remember: Add fractions only after finding a common denominator.

candidates.subskill: Intersections of a line and a parabola
candidates.stem: The graphs of y = x² and y = 2x + 3 intersect at two points. What is the sum of the x-coordinates of the two intersection points?
candidates.explanation: Setting x² = 2x + 3 gives x² − 2x − 3 = 0, so (x − 3)(x + 1) = 0 and x = 3 or x = −1. The sum is 2.

A.rationale: −3 is the product of the x-coordinates, not their sum.

C.rationale: 3 is only one of the x-coordinates.

D.rationale: 4 adds 3 and 1, dropping the negative sign of −1.

hints: Solve the quadratic, then add the solutions.
candidates.remember: Intersections: set the equations equal and solve.

author_checklist.hardness: two-step setup; sign and product traps

candidates.stem: A shop rents bicycles for $8 per hour. Each rental also has a $5 helmet fee, and members receive a $3 discount on the total. Which expression gives the total cost, in dollars, for a member who rents a bicycle for h hours?

A.rationale: This leaves out the $5 helmet fee.

B.rationale: This adds the discount instead of subtracting it.

C.rationale: This charges the helmet fee per hour.

hints: Which charges depend on h, and which are one-time?
candidates.remember: Separate per-unit charges from one-time charges.

candidates.stem: The value V, in dollars, of a machine t years after purchase is modeled by V(t) = 500(0.9)^t. Which statement best describes the meaning of 0.9 in this model?

choices.A: The machine loses $0.90 of its value each year.
choices.B: The machine's value decreases by 90% each year.
choices.C: The machine's value increases by 10% each year.
choices.D: The machine's value decreases by 10% each year.

candidates.explanation: Each year the value is multiplied by 0.9, so it keeps 90% and loses 10% of its value.

A.rationale: The model multiplies by 0.9; it does not subtract $0.90.

C.rationale: A factor less than 1 means the value decreases.

hints: What happens to the value from t = 0 to t = 1?
candidates.remember: A growth factor b means a change of (b − 1) × 100%.

candidates.stem: The function g is defined by g(x) = f(2x). If f(6) = 10, for what value of x must g(x) equal 10 ?
candidates.explanation: g(x) = f(2x) equals f(6) when 2x = 6, so x = 3.

B.rationale: 6 assumes g and f give the same output at the same input.

hints: What input to f does g(x) = f(2x) use?
candidates.remember: f(2x) compresses horizontally: inputs are halved.

author_checklist.hardness: horizontal stretch runs opposite to intuition; most double

candidates.subskill: Circumscribed circle of a right triangle
candidates.stem: A right triangle has legs of length 10 and 24. What is the radius of the circle that passes through all three vertices of the triangle?
candidates.explanation: The hypotenuse is √(10² + 24²) = 26. In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is a diameter of the circumscribed circle, so the radius is 13.

A.rationale: 12 is half of the longer leg.

D.rationale: 26 is the diameter (the hypotenuse), not the radius.

hints: What is special about the hypotenuse of a right triangle inscribed in a circle?

strategy.explanation: The right angle subtends a semicircle.

candidates.remember: A right triangle's hypotenuse is a diameter of its circumcircle.

author_checklist.hardness: requires the semicircle (Thales) fact; diameter trap

candidates.stem: A line with slope 3 passes through the points (2, k) and (5, 11). What is the value of k ?

A.rationale: −7 uses a run of 6 instead of 3: 11 − 18.

B.rationale: −2 makes a sign error solving 11 − k = 9.

hints: Write the slope formula with k.

candidates.subskill: Probability that a specific person is chosen
candidates.stem: Three people are chosen at random from a group of 8 people to form a committee. What is the probability that Ana, one of the 8, is chosen?
candidates.explanation: Committees including Ana: C(7, 2) = 21. All committees: C(8, 3) = 56. Probability = 21/56 = 3/8. (Equivalently, 3 of the 8 spots are filled.)

A.rationale: 1/8 is the chance Ana is picked for one specific seat, not any of three.

B.rationale: 1/4 has no basis in the setup.

D.rationale: 1/2 assumes Ana is either chosen or not with equal chance.

candidates.remember: Each person's chance equals spots ÷ people.

candidates.stem: In a large data set summarized by a box plot, the third quartile is 84. Approximately what percent of the data values are greater than 84 ?
candidates.explanation: The third quartile marks the 75th percentile, so about 25% of values lie above it.

B.rationale: 50% lies above the median, not the third quartile.

C.rationale: 75% lies below the third quartile, not above it.

D.rationale: 84 is the value itself, not a percent.

hints: What percent of data lies below Q3?
candidates.remember: Q1, median, Q3 split the data into quarters.

candidates.stem: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour and 2 eggs for each batch. A baker has 10 cups of flour and 8 eggs. What is the greatest number of complete batches the baker can make?
candidates.explanation: Flour allows 10 ÷ 3 = 3 complete batches; eggs allow 8 ÷ 2 = 4. The flour runs out first, so 3 batches.

B.rationale: 4 uses only the eggs and ignores that flour runs out.

C.rationale: 5 divides 10 cups by 2 (the eggs per batch), mixing up the ingredients.

D.rationale: 6 adds the flour and egg limits.

hints: How many batches does each ingredient allow?
candidates.remember: The scarcest ingredient limits the total.
